newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods gain on ACCESS after APIs.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods gain on ACCESS after APIs.

text.p: U.S. spot refined products prices gained moderately in after-hours ACCESS trade late Tuesday on new weekly API data, although some cash traders declared the data mildly bearish for East Coast heating oil.
February heating oil futures edged 0.28 cent a gallon higher in ACCESS trade, while February gasoline jumped a half cent by 1745 EST (2245 GMT) after release of the data for the week ending Jan 10.
They showed distillates slipping by 1.3 million barrels a day, with heating oil stocks falling 1.8 million -- including a moderate 309,000 barrel draw in the key East Coast market.

The data showed total East Coast heating oil stocks down 3.2 million barrels from the same week in January 1996 -- a vast improvement over last week's API report showing a 6.5 million barrel shortfall from the comparable 1996 period.
The closing of the gap can be explained in part by the contrast between last year's cold winter and the relatively mild temperatures experienced so far this year.

One Gulf Coast trader labelled the heating oil data bearish, saying over 45 percent of the U.S. draw was in the Gulf Coast, much of it from exports. "East Coast demand stinks. I wouldn't buy the market," he said.
